full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that the petitioner Nos. 1-2, 12-14 and the predecessor of the petitioner Nos.3-11 as plaintiffs instituted Civil Suit No. 118 of 1988 subsequently (re-numbered as Civil Suit No. 132 of 1994) before the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla for declaration of Title alleging that the suit land appertaining to CS Khatian No.11 corresponding to Hal Khatian No. 40 of Mouja Porkara under Police Station Chowddagram originally belonged to Dula Mia and his brother namely-Sekandar Ali with equal 8 annas share, for arrears of rent superior landlord obtained decree in rent suit without serving any notice and one Abdul Hakim shown to be auction purchaser. Abdul Hakim never obtained possession in pursuance of the decree passed in the rent suit. Dula Mia and his brother remained in possession of the suit property as before. Subsequently, Dula Mia filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 161 of 1939 for setting aside the auction and Abdul Hakim filed Civil Suit No. 19 of 1939 against Dula Mia and his brother Sekandar Ali and their mother for possession of the auction purchased land. Both the suits were disposed of in accordance with solenama and in terms of solenama 45 decimals of land were given settlement in favour of Sekandar Ali and Dula Mia from RS Plot No.415. Abdul Hakim Majumder settled 96 decimals of land by way of unregistered patta dated 15-10-1948 in favour of Dula Mia at Selami of Taka 145 but in the patta wrongly RS Plot No.415 written and possession was given on RS Plot No.1246 in favour of Dula Mia. Dula Mia remained in possession of the property under plot No.1246 entirely and 8 annas share of land under plot No.3 and paid rents for schedule Nos. 1, 2, 4, 6 and for half share of RS Plot No.415 of schedule No. 3. 

 5. Sekandar Ali and Dula Mia never got settlement of 45 decimals of land equally and possessed accordingly. Sekandar Ali filed objection under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure against that execution case and that was dismissed on hearing and against that Appeal No.82 of 1943 was preferred by Sekandar Ali and that appeal was also disallowed on 17.08.1943. The claim of the plaintiff is that he obtained 96 decimals of land by way of patta dated 15-10-1948 is quite false and fictitious. Abdul Hakim Majumder never executed any patta deed in favour of Dula Mia. Plaintiff never obtained any suit property by way of Solenama and also did not obtain any property by registered deed dated 2-1-1976. The claim of the plaintiff is quite false and fictitious. The predecessor of the defendant Abdul Hakim obtained the suit property by auction purchase and obtained possession and during their possession the plaintiff and Sekandar Ali trespassed into the land comprising 19 decimals under plot Nos. 360 and 361 and subsequently got registered deed dated 25-6-1976 from the defendant No.1 and obtained possession of 6 decimals of land. Abdul Hakim Majumder filed Title Suit No.57 of 1988 for recovery of khas possession of 13 decimals of land in the court of Nangalkot and the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed. 

 15. He further submits that after institution of the suit for declaration of title the plaintiff by way of amendment prayed for a decree by way of adverse possession and in support of their claim PW 1 in his deposition and cross-examination asserted that their predecessor was in possession of the suit land by way of settlement and patta and they are in possession also and as a whole they are in possession about 60 years in the suit land. Other P.Ws. corroborated the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 and thus the plaintiffs proved their case that they are in possession in the suit land since CS operation and it was proved by the report of the Revenue Officer that the objection raised by the defendants was rejected as such the plaintiffs have been able to prove their case. On the other hand, the defendants though produced some documents before the court but by adducing oral evidence they could not prove their possession in the suit land. Both the courts below on mis-appreciation of the facts and circumstances of the case mis-construed the same and arrived at a wrong decision in dismissing the suit of the plaintiff by which committed an error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 18. He further submits that the defendants by adducing oral and documentary evidence prove their case that they have title and possession in the suit land, as they have got possession through Court, the defendant also established their claim that the alleged un-registered patta has no existence at all and on consideration of this fact both the Courts below found title and possession of the defendants in the suit land. So, the claim of the plaintiffs of adverse possession is not established in any form of evidence both oral and documentary and on consideration the aforesaid oral and documentary evidence of the trial court and the appellate court concurrently found that the defendants are in possession on the suit land and the plaintiffs have no title and possession on the suit land and dismissed the suit as well as the appeal. Thus, the concurrent findings of fact arrived at by the Courts below cannot be interfered with by the Revisional jurisdiction in the facts and circumstances of the case. He prayed for discharged of the Rule. 

 21. On perusal of the record it appears that the predecessor of the Plaintiff-Petitioners namely Dula Mia and his brother namely Sekander Ali were the original owners of the suit land evidencing from the CS Khatian (Exhibit-1(Ka)) and RS Khatian (Exhbit-1). The predecessor of the Plaintiff-Petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 161 of 1939 for settlement. The predecessor of the Defendants-Opposite Parties No. 1-3 instituted Civil Suit No. 19 of 1939 for recovery of khas possession. The suit was decreed on 11-10-1939 on Solenama (Exhibit-2) according to Solenama, 0.45 acre were settled to Dula Mia and Sekender Ali. As per terms of Solenama Suit land was settled to Dula Mia vide registered patta dated 15-10-1948 and Partly Settlement Khatian No. 151 was recorded for Dula Mia and after SAT Act coming into force, Dula Mia became owner of the Suit land under the Government and RS Khatian (Exhibit-1) was recorded in the name of Dula Mia and he paid rents (Exhibit-3 series). 

 22. The suit land was put in auction and the predecessor of the defendants-opposite party Nos.1-3 namely Abdul Hakim auction purchased the suit land. On prayer of the predecessor of the petitioner namely Dula Mia, Abdul Hakim settled 96 acres schedule land vide registered patta dated 15-10-1948 in favour of the Dula Mia from CS Plot Nos. 363, 365, 415, 418, 329, 327. 

 (ii) Patta dated 15-10-1948 shows that it was executed in terms of the sole decree. 

 (iii) The ownership, possession and also settlement patta of 96 decimals of land in favour of Dula Mia were proved by petty settlement khatian 11/1 recording the name of Dula Mia in the Khatian. 

 The above order clearly established the possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land from the time of their predecessor. (vi) PW 1 deposed in the suit that Abdus Hakim Majumder could not go into possession of the suit land. Plaintiff in their pleading claimed adverse possession. PW 1 in his deposition claimed decree on the basis of adverse possession PW 2 deposed that plaintiffs and their predecessor have been possessing the suit land and that defendants never possessed the suit land and never evicted the plaintiffs from the suit land PW 3 corroborated PWs 1 and 2 in respect of plaintiffs and their predecessor's possession in the suit land. The oral and documentary evidence conclusively proves that the plaintiff-predecessors were in possession of the suit land since the time of CS record and possession was not ever taken from them by the predecessor of the defendants and the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land from the time of their predecessors. The trial court and the lower appellate Court have misread the evidence, oral and documentary and did not consider oral and documentary evidence while dismissing the suit filed by the plaintiffs. (vii) The unregistered patta executed by Abdul Hakim Majumder filed by the plaintiff was kept in safe custody where damaged the same, but the lower appellate court has drawn an adverse inference against the plaintiffs most arbitrarily to the effect that the damage was caused by the plaintiffs without considering that nobody will take any action to destroy his own evidence and this shows that the lower appellant court failed to apply its judicial mind to the facts of this case. 

 29. The patta executed by Abdul Hakim Majumder (defendants predecessor) in favour of Dula Mia, son of Late Bande Ali (plaintiff's predecessor) shows that about Hakim Majumder executed patta dated 15-10-1948 settling 96 decimals of land in favour of the Dula Mia according to the terms of sole decree in civil Suit No. 19 of 1939. The ownership, and possession and also settlement of Dula Mia in 96 decimals of land are also evidenced from the petty settlement Khatian No. 11/1 recording the name of Dula Mia in the khatian. 

 36. In the present case if it is found that the patta granting settlement in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor is defective then in view of continues adverse possession of the plaintiffs from their predecessors for more than 60 years prior to the institution of the suit as evidenced form the rent receipts and oral and documentary evidence has conferred indefeasible title on the plaintiffs. 

 41. In the present case, since the unregistered patta was accompanied by delivery of possession the lease is valid for one year and the plaintiffs and their predecessors having continued in possession with the assent of the lessor the plaintiffs became tenants by holding over under section 116 of the Transfer of property Act. So even if the unregistered patta is treated as lease for one year, lease continued by the possession of the plaintiffs and their predecessors and therefore, they became tenants in the suit land by holding over under section 116 of the Transfer of property Act. Hence, the settlement in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessor is valid and the plaintiffs being in lawful possession has acquired title in the suit land.
